title: Affective Involvement
role_in_volume: DIMENSION CHAPTER — affective dimension of the 6-dim Player Involvement Model. Volume's SHORTEST dimension chapter (12 pp.) and structurally sparsest (3 named subsections vs 4-5 in peers). Confirmed-under-developed per Phase 0 along four axes (page count, subsection count, emotion-theory citation density, theoretical-framework absence). Per plan §1.4 and §1 of this Phase 2 brief, this is the volume's PREMIER dissertation-augmentation site: Gross 2017 (Uncomfortable Situations, confirmed corpus-index pipeline) + Aristotelian pathē + Burke pentadic Attitude + Uexküllian Merktöne/Wirktöne can substantively extend rather than merely re-describe Calleja's affective treatment.

outline.title: Macro Phase: Escapism and Affect
outline.summary: Opens with the cybernetic-feedback-loop premise (cognitive + emotional + kinesthetic) as the medium-specific basis for digital games' affective intensity (lines 4729-4738). Bryant + Davies 2006 and Grodal 2000 are co-cited at line 4738 to evidentiate that games are 'a particularly powerful medium for affecting players' moods and emotional states' — these are the chapter's only two emotion-theory citations. The 'excitatory homeostasis' construct (Bryant + Davies 2006, p.183) is introduced at lines 4748-4761 as the media-psychology framework for how players regulate arousal via game choice and difficulty-setting tweaks. The first occurrence of 'rhetorical strategies of affect' appears at lines 4762-4764 in the context of game design as imbued with affective rhetoric, augmented by the recursive input/output loop's extension of non-ergodic rhetoric. The escapism apparatus then occupies the bulk of the macro phase (lines 4770-4910): the escape/escapism distinction (lines 4778-4795 — escape = permanent one-way move, escapism = round-trip), the imagination-as-faculty-of-escapism premise (lines 4814-4822), the Tuan 1998 block quote on humans as animals 'congenitally indisposed to accept reality' and culture as 'seeing what is not there' (lines 4824-4831), the Tuan 'local pattern or order' definition of the real (lines 4832-4845), the relativization-of-escapism argument (lines 4846-4858 — the baker-rockstar/musician-baker symmetry), the Oriel-on-Menethil-Harbor aesthetic-habitation testimony (lines 4867-4873), the Tolkien 1983 'secondary worlds' block quote (lines 4883-4889), and the Tolkien 'Escape of the Prisoner vs Flight of the Deserter' defense (lines 4894-4905). The Macro Phase closes by positing digital games as continuators of secondary-world creation, with MMOGs extending this via persistence + synchronous-shared experience (lines 4906-4911).

outline.title: Micro Phase: Emotional Affect during Gameplay
outline.summary: Pivots to moment-to-moment affective response during play. Opens with the designed-vs-precipitated affect distinction (lines 4913-4927): designers cannot dictate specific effects but design choices encourage particular reactions. The 'mode of representation' argument (lines 4928-4933) posits graphics+sound as evocative — qualified against the anti-graphical-power consensus among certain theorists+designers (unnamed). The Inauro-on-Duskwood-as-Mirkwood testimony (lines 4934-4939) supplies the chapter's clearest atmospherics-as-affect exhibit: lighting + sound + monster placement + thematic consistency. The verisimilitude-vs-media-pastiche distinction is introduced via the Medal of Honor : Allied Assault (Hollywood-pastiche, drawing on Saving Private Ryan + Pearl Harbor) vs Red Orchestra: Ostfront 41-45 (historical-accuracy) paradigm case (lines 4956-4991). Red Orchestra's design choices — no crosshairs (line 4976), iron-sights requirement, prone/kneel for recoil compensation, bolt-action single-shot rifles (line 4983) — exemplify how mechanics-encoded historical-accuracy generates a distinct affective register. The suppressing-fire-as-apprehension-paradigm (lines 4992-5018) closes the micro phase: combining graphical distortion + loud audio + environmental physics generates 'a heightened sense of urgency, if not panic' in opposition players, with screen blur/shake when leaning out to return fire, dust+fragments from destructible cover, and historically-accurate weapon-inaccuracy compounding the affective effect. This is Calleja's clearest exhibit of designed affect at the mechanic level.

outline.title: Aesthetics and Affect
outline.summary: Swing-section bridging Macro (escapism / aesthetic habitation) and Micro (moment-to-moment designed affect). Opens with the Aprile-on-Night-Elf-Land testimony (lines 5022-5027): the 'serene and pretty' Teldrassil temple as mood-regulation site visited 'whenever I don't feel like playing.' Calleja explicates the WoW designers' aesthetic strategy (lines 5028-5036): persistent worlds require positive-emotion-inspiring places to sustain extended participation, hence varying palettes of 'tastefully blended colors' and a design policy of broad appeal. The horror-affect counterweight begins at line 5037 with F.E.A.R. (Monolith 2005) as the action-horror paradigm: linear plot, environment-explorable, alternating combat-and-paranormal-horror sequences (lines 5040-5052). Adaptive-AI affective intensity is described via F.E.A.R.'s AI agents who duck, take cover, collaborate, and flank from behind (lines 5053-5073); flanking attacks are reactive (not predetermined or area-triggered) and induce an alerted state that 'leads to a more intense engagement in the spatial and ludic involvement dimensions' (lines 5071-5073) — a paradigm cross-dimensional-affective-amplification observation. The horror sequences (lines 5074-5085) describe the swaying/flickering light bulbs, the scampering-child-on-all-fours sudden-appearance, and the way prior combat-intensity amplifies subsequent horror — generating 'an intensified sense of shock and uncanniness.' The Left 4 Dead 2 (Valve 2009) AI-'director' paradigm follows (lines 5086-5123): the director generates enemies+weapons+ammo+objects to calibrate dramatic tension; audio+visual+character-voiceover segments add to the 'tense and dark atmosphere'; cooperative-panic affect via Hunter-zombie special abilities that require teammate-rescue, with 'players shouting to their friends to save them' under simultaneous attack. Line 5119 contains the chapter's second occurrence of 'rhetorical strategies of affect.' The section closes (lines 5124-5151) with a typology of affective-experience options (high-adrenaline horror; peaceful aesthetics; media-pastiche visual style; startling-effect exhilaration), the Salen+Zimmerman 2003 invocation as foil for the 'representational-affective design as legitimate aim' defense, and the closing characterization of digital games as 'digitally mediated experiences that aim to satisfy the desires generated by movies, literature, or free-ranging fantasy.'

outline.title: (Unnamed closing coda)
outline.summary: Two-paragraph dimension-recapitulation: the affective-involvement dimension 'encompasses various forms of emotional engagement, ranging from the calming sensation of happening upon an aesthetically soothing scene, the adrenaline rush of an on-line competitive first-person shooter, or the uncanny effect of an eerie episode in an action-horror game.' Line 5156 contains the chapter's THIRD occurrence of 'rhetorical strategies of affect' — the dimension is here defined as 'accounting for' those strategies, whether designer-purposed or player-precipitated. The designed-vs-precipitated distinction (introduced at S2 opening) here receives its terminological codification as the dimension's signature analytic move.

concepts.label: Cybernetic feedback loop (cognitive + emotional + kinesthetic)
concepts.note: Medium-specific basis for digital-game affective intensity; the three-channel formulation appears once and is not re-theorized.

concepts.label: Excitatory homeostasis (Bryant + Davies 2006)
concepts.note: Sole imported emotion-construct in the chapter; media-psychology in register, not affect-theoretic; framed as arousal-regulation via entertainment choice.

concepts.label: Rhetorical strategies of affect
concepts.note: Triple-invocation across the chapter without any rhetorical-theoretic-tradition citation (no Burke, no Aristotle, no Hawhee). STRONGEST single anticipatory anchor in the volume per propagated IG-03/IG-10 finding.

concepts.label: Mood-affecting qualities of games
concepts.note: Calleja uses 'mood' and 'emotional state' as paired-noun construction throughout; the mood/emotion distinction (theoretically load-bearing in affect theory — Heidegger Stimmung, Massumi affect/emotion split, Barrett constructed-emotion) is absent. Conflation, not theorization.

concepts.label: Escapism vs escape distinction (round-trip vs one-way)
concepts.note: Calleja's foundational conceptual move in the Macro phase. Escape = permanent one-way move; escapism = movement-with-return-expectation.

concepts.label: Imagination as the human faculty enabling escapism
concepts.note: Mental imagery permits retention of past + potential future + present awareness simultaneously; 'seeing what is not there' (Tuan 1998, 5-6). Paradigmatic phantasia operation in classical-rhetorical register, though Calleja does not name it phantasia.

concepts.label: The real as 'local pattern or order' (Tuan 1998)
concepts.note: Tuan's definition of the real: legibility / decreased contingency; both natural and designed belong to the real; interpretability is the determinant.

concepts.label: Secondary worlds (Tolkien 1983)
concepts.note: 'Inner consistency of reality' as the structural property enabling habitation; 'willing suspension of disbelief' critique block-quoted; MMOGs as continuators-with-persistence.

concepts.label: Escape of the Prisoner vs Flight of the Deserter (Tolkien)
concepts.note: Tolkien's defense of escapism against academic scorn; deployed as Calleja's escapism-defense apparatus alongside Tuan and Evans 2001.

concepts.label: Designed vs precipitated affect
concepts.note: Designers cannot dictate specific effects but design choices encourage particular reactions; player interpretation + interruptions + interest variance produce precipitated rather than designed responses. Coda terminologizes this as the dimension's signature.

concepts.label: Atmospherics (lighting + sound + monster placement + thematic consistency)
concepts.note: Inauro's Duskwood/Mirkwood/Silverpine testimony; paradigmatic Umwelt-with-tones exhibit (Uexküllian anticipatory anchor).

concepts.label: Verisimilitude vs media-pastiche affective registers
concepts.note: Medal of Honor (Hollywood-pastiche, drawing on Saving Private Ryan + Pearl Harbor) vs Red Orchestra (historical-accuracy + iron-sights + bolt-action). Two ostensibly similar games producing 'very different affective experiences.' Paradigm case for the chapter.

concepts.label: Suppressing fire as designed affect-generation mechanic
concepts.note: Graphical distortion + loud audio + environmental physics + destructible cover generating apprehension, urgency, near-panic. The chapter's clearest mechanic-level designed-affect exhibit.

concepts.label: Aesthetic mood-regulation (WoW landscape design)
concepts.note: Aprile-on-Night-Elf-Land; persistent worlds require positive-emotion places; varying palettes / tasteful blending; broad-appeal design policy.

concepts.label: Negative affect as legitimate involvement
concepts.note: Frustration, panic, fear, eeriness, shock, uncanny — all treated as legitimate affective involvement; 'better than experiencing boredom.' Heightens other dimensions in certain cases. Under-theorized (no Berlant cruel-optimism, no Ngai ugly feelings, no Aristotelian pathē of fear-pity).

concepts.label: Cross-dimensional affective amplification
concepts.note: Repeatedly observed but not theorized: affect heightens spatial + ludic + shared involvement and vice versa. F.E.A.R. flanking-AI heightens spatial+ludic; Left 4 Dead 2 cooperative-panic combines aesthetic+systemic dimensions.

concepts.label: Adaptive AI 'director' (Left 4 Dead 2)
concepts.note: Generates enemies + weapons + ammo + objects to calibrate dramatic tension; audio+visual+voiceover modulation; sends zombie hordes when players 'appear too relaxed.' Paradigm case of dynamic affect-modulation systems.

concepts.label: Shock and uncanniness (F.E.A.R. horror sequences)
concepts.note: Swaying/flickering light bulbs + scampering-child sudden-appearance + objects flying off shelves; prior combat-intensity amplifies subsequent horror. Calleja does not invoke Freud's Unheimlich despite using 'uncanny.'

concepts.label: Packaged experience (digitally mediated satisfaction of desires from movies / literature / fantasy)
concepts.note: Closing-section anti-mechanics-purism move; foiled against Salen + Zimmerman 2003; digital games as digitally-mediated experiences.

concepts.label: Habitable secondary-world as affective space
concepts.note: Oriel-on-Menethil-Harbor testimony ('I want to live there') + Tolkien secondary-worlds bridge; aesthetic habitation as affective-involvement driver.

concepts.label: Under-developed-dimension status (substantive observation)
concepts.note: Phase 2 finding: the chapter is the volume's shortest dimension treatment, structurally sparsest (3 subsections), citation-density-sparsest (2 emotion-theory cites, 1 construct), and theoretically thinnest (no affect-theory, no cognitive-emotion-science, no phenomenology of mood). This sparsity is itself a substantive observation per Phase 2 special guidance and the volume's premier dissertation-augmentation site per plan §1.4.

positions.label: Affect is the emotional-tonal modulation of involvement, generated via the cybernetic feedback loop and crystallized as 'rhetorical strategies' built into game design
positions.summary: Calleja's core thesis: digital games are particularly powerful affect-media because the cognitive + emotional + kinesthetic feedback loop produces recursive input/output that extends the non-ergodic rhetoric of textual production into a domain where 'rhetorical strategies of affect' modulate both designed and precipitated player response. The dimension is the tonality-of-involvement across all other five dimensions.

positions.label: Escapism is a legitimate, defensible cultural-imaginative activity — not a derogatory term
positions.summary: Aligned with Tuan 1998 + Tolkien 1983 + Evans 2001 against academics who use 'escape' or 'escapism' with scorn or pity. The escape/escapism distinction (round-trip vs one-way), the relativization-of-escapism argument (no activity is essentially escapist), and the Tolkien Prisoner-vs-Deserter framing converge to establish escapism as the human-imaginative faculty's normal exercise, with digital games as legitimate continuators of secondary-world creation.

positions.label: Both designed and precipitated affect count as affective involvement
positions.summary: Designed affect = designer-purposed emotional responses encoded via mechanics + atmospherics + AI behavior. Precipitated affect = player-interpretation-generated responses (including those that diverge from designer intent or that arise from interruptions, lack of interest, or context). The dimension accounts for both; the distinction itself is Calleja's terminological signature for the dimension.

positions.label: Representational-affective design is a legitimate aim alongside mechanic innovation
positions.summary: Against Salen + Zimmerman 2003 (and a broader designer-theorist 'representation-at-cost-of-design' suspicion), Calleja defends representational-affective design as legitimate because digital games are 'not only game systems but, more importantly, are digitally mediated experiences that aim to satisfy the desires generated by movies, literature, or free-ranging fantasy.' The packaged-experience defense is the closing move.

positions.label: Chapter-as-under-developed-dimension — substantive observation, not description-deficit
positions.summary: PROPAGATED FROM IG-03 + IG-10 FINDINGS. This Phase 2 deep-analysis explicitly documents the chapter's under-developed status as a substantive analytic finding: only 2 emotion-theory citations (Bryant + Davies 2006; Grodal 2000) supplying only 1 imported construct (excitatory homeostasis); zero engagement with affect theory (Massumi, Sedgwick, Berlant, Ahmed, Ngai), cognitive-emotion-science (Damasio — present in Ch.10 but absent here; Ekman, Frijda, Plutchik, Barrett, Barsalou, Tomkins), or phenomenology of mood (Heidegger Stimmung); the mood/emotion distinction is conflated rather than theorized; cross-dimensional affective amplification is repeatedly observed but never mechanism-theorized; 'rhetorical strategies of affect' is triple-invoked without any rhetorical-theoretic tradition (Burke, Aristotle, Hawhee). The chapter's primary conceptual interlocutor is Yi-Fu Tuan — a geographer of place and imagination, not an emotion theorist. The escapism-defense apparatus (Tuan + Tolkien + Evans) occupies roughly the first 4-5 of 12 pages. This sparsity is corroborated at four levels: (a) page count (shortest dimension chapter), (b) subsection count (3 named vs 4-5 in peers), (c) emotion-theory citation density (1 construct vs Ch.4's 7-8 interlocutors), (d) theoretical-framework absence. The chapter is consequently the volume's PREMIER dissertation-augmentation site.

positions.label: Cross-dimensional affective amplification is a recurrent but un-theorized phenomenon
positions.summary: Three discrete passages observe that affect heightens spatial + ludic + shared involvement and vice versa (frustration-as-engagement-driver; F.E.A.R. flanking-AI heightens spatial+ludic; Left 4 Dead 2 cooperative-panic combines aesthetic+systemic). Yet Calleja supplies no mechanism-theory for how cross-dimensional affective amplification works. This is a paradigm augmentation hook for Gross 2017 (situated-affect frame) and/or for a Burkean Attitude-as-modulator-of-pentad-terms reading.

tensions.label: Atmospherics-as-affect-source vs rules/mechanics-as-affect-source
tensions.summary: The chapter holds two distinct accounts of where designed affect originates. On one account, affect emerges from atmospherics — lighting, sound, monster placement, thematic consistency (Inauro Duskwood passage); aesthetic palette and tasteful blending (WoW landscape design); the visual+audio mode of representation. On the other, affect emerges from mechanics — Red Orchestra's no-crosshairs + iron-sights + bolt-action + suppressing-fire generates apprehension via gameplay constraints, not via prettiness; F.E.A.R.'s flanking AI generates alertness via behavior, not appearance. Calleja's Left 4 Dead 2 closing observation that 'rhetorical strategies of affect tightly combine the aesthetic and systemic dimensions' (line 5119) acknowledges the dual sourcing but does not resolve it into a unified theory. Resolved (anticipatorily) by Gross 2017 situated-conceptualization frame OR by Uexküllian Merktöne/Wirktöne dual-tone doctrine which natively integrates perception-side and action-side affective tonality.

tensions.label: Emotion-via-avatar vs emotion-as-player
tensions.summary: Some affective passages locate emotion in the player as such (Oriel's 'I want to live there'; Aprile's 'It's calming'; the baker-dreaming-of-rock-stardom relativization). Other affective passages presuppose emotion mediated through avatar-embodiment (F.E.A.R. flanking attacks 'leave players in an alerted state'; Left 4 Dead 2 Hunter knockdown 'creates considerable panic'; suppressing-fire generates apprehension 'in the opposition players'). The transition between these two registers is not theorized — Calleja does not distinguish proprioceptive-avatar-grounded affect from observer-affect-at-aesthetic-distance. This tension is anticipatorily resolvable through (a) Uexküllian Wirkmal-coupling (the avatar as the player's effector-organ-in-Umwelt), (b) Aristotelian pathē-via-rhetorical-strategy (where the rhetorical situation produces patterned response regardless of avatar mediation), or (c) Gross 2017 situated-affect grounding (the situation including avatar-as-mediator precipitates the response).

tensions.label: Mood as steady-state-environmental vs emotion as event-discrete
tensions.summary: Calleja uses 'mood' and 'emotion(al state)' interchangeably ('moods and emotional states' as paired-noun construction at lines 4737, 4753, 4861). Yet the chapter's examples actually fall on two sides of the mood/emotion distinction that affect theory treats as load-bearing: the WoW aesthetic-mood-regulation passages (Aprile's calming Night Elf Land, Oriel's peaceful Menethil Harbor) instantiate mood-as-environmental-attunement, while the F.E.A.R. flanking + Left 4 Dead 2 Hunter-attack passages instantiate emotion-as-event-discrete. The conflation flattens what Heidegger's Stimmung analysis, Massumi's affect/emotion split, and Barrett's constructed-emotion theory all theorize as a foundational distinction. Anticipatorily addressed by BCAP Stimmung-doctrine + Gross 2017 mood-as-Berlant-impasse-affect.

game_loci.title: World of Warcraft
game_loci.role: Recurring affective-aesthetic anchor site. Oriel at Menethil Harbor (lines 4867-4873, sunset / boat-waiting / Gadgetzan-night-flying / Winterspring-snow-crunching / Azshara-leaves); Inauro on Duskwood Forest / Silverpine Forest / Brill (lines 4934-4939, 'so Mirkwood from The Hobbit'); Aprile on Night Elf Land / Teldrassil temple (lines 5022-5027, 'serene and pretty,' 'calming'); Figure 8.1 = Teldrassil interview event. Anchor for aesthetic-habitation-as-affect, mood-regulation-via-environment, atmospherics paradigm.

game_loci.title: Medal of Honor: Allied Assault
game_loci.role: Hollywood-pastiche verisimilitude exemplar (lines 4964-4970). Visual style draws on Saving Private Ryan + Pearl Harbor. Crosshair-equipped; movement-shoot accurate. Paired with Red Orchestra as paradigm case for verisimilitude-vs-pastiche affective registers.

game_loci.title: Red Orchestra: Ostfront 41-45
game_loci.role: Historical-accuracy + iron-sights affective register exemplar (lines 4971-4991). No crosshairs; bolt-action single-shot rifles; prone/kneel for recoil compensation; uniform/weapon/object historical fidelity. Suppressing-fire-as-apprehension paradigm (lines 4992-5019): graphical distortion + loud audio + destructible-cover physics + iron-sights aiming generates urgency-near-panic.

game_loci.title: Counter-Strike: Source
game_loci.role: Comparator for shoot-while-moving affective tempo (line 4979). Foiled against Red Orchestra's prone-kneel-required design.

game_loci.title: F.E.A.R.
game_loci.role: Action-FPS + horror paradigm (lines 5037-5085). Linear plot, environment-explorable, alternating combat / paranormal-horror / plot-furthering-terror sequences. Adaptive-AI agents (duck, cover, collaborate, flanking from behind) generate alerted-state engagement, heightening spatial + ludic dimensions. Horror sequences: swaying/flickering light bulbs, scampering-child-on-all-fours, objects flying off shelves — generating shock + uncanniness.

game_loci.title: F.E.A.R. 2: Project Origin
game_loci.role: Startling-sequence paradigm (Figure 8.2, p.144; lines 5086-5087). Unpredictable AI applied with 'even greater emotional effect.' Anchor for the AI-unpredictability-as-affect-generator argument.

game_loci.title: Left 4 Dead 2
game_loci.role: Adaptive-AI 'director' paradigm (lines 5086-5123). Director generates enemies + weapons + ammo + objects to calibrate dramatic tension; audio+visual+voiceover modulation; sends zombie hordes when players 'appear too relaxed'; Hunter special-zombie knockdown requires teammate-rescue → cooperative-panic affect. Calleja's clearest statement of 'rhetorical strategies of affect tightly combine the aesthetic and systemic dimensions' (line 5119) is anchored here.

game_loci.title: Saving Private Ryan
game_loci.role: Film referent for Medal of Honor visual style (line 4967). Anchors the media-pastiche affective register category.

game_loci.title: Pearl Harbor
game_loci.role: Film referent for Medal of Honor visual style (line 4967). Anchors the media-pastiche affective register category.

game_loci.title: The Hobbit / Mirkwood
game_loci.role: Literary referent for Duskwood Forest aesthetic, via Inauro's participant quote (lines 4934-4935). Anchors the secondary-world-aesthetic-evocation-as-affect category. Tolkien 1983 'On Fairy Stories' is the theoretical source elsewhere in the chapter (block-quoted lines 4883-4889, 4894-4905).

interlocutors.name: Jennings Bryant and John Davies
interlocutors.work: (2006) Selective Exposure to Video Games (in Vorderer + Bryant eds., Playing Video Games)
interlocutors.role: PRIMARY emotion-theoretic citation, but supplying only ONE construct (excitatory homeostasis, p.183). Cited at line 4738 (mood-affecting media argument) and line 4750 (excitatory homeostasis definition). Media-psychology in register; not affect-theory or cognitive-emotion-science.

interlocutors.name: Torben Grodal
interlocutors.work: (2000) Video Games and the Pleasures of Control (in Zillmann + Vorderer eds., Media Entertainment)
interlocutors.role: Co-cited with Bryant + Davies at line 4738 as evidence that games are 'a particularly powerful medium for affecting players' moods and emotional states.' No further engagement, no extended quotation, no theoretical development. Tier-C citation despite Grodal being a major theorist of film+game emotion (Embodied Visions etc.).

interlocutors.name: Yi-Fu Tuan
interlocutors.role: PRIMARY conceptual interlocutor for the Macro Phase. Supplies (a) the escapism-as-cultural-imagination frame, (b) the human-as-animal-indisposed-to-accept-reality definition (block-quote lines 4824-4831), (c) the 'local pattern or order' definition of the real (block-quote lines 4842-4845). NOT an emotion theorist proper — Tuan is a geographer of place + imagination. Calleja's principal Macro-phase voice.

interlocutors.name: J. R. R. Tolkien
interlocutors.role: Supplies (a) 'inner consistency of reality' (line 4776), (b) 'secondary worlds' / 'willing suspension of disbelief' critique (block-quote lines 4883-4889), (c) Escape-of-the-Prisoner-vs-Flight-of-the-Deserter defense of escapism (block-quote lines 4894-4905). Escapism-defense interlocutor, not emotion theorist.

interlocutors.name: Andrew Evans
interlocutors.work: (2001) This Virtual Life: Escapism in the Media
interlocutors.role: Aligned with Tuan + Tolkien at line 4892 in rejecting scornful uses of 'escape.' Light citation; functions as third member of the escapism-defense apparatus.

interlocutors.name: Katie Salen and Eric Zimmerman
interlocutors.role: Cited at line 5139 as 'among a number of game designers who have expressed doubt about the trend toward improving representation at the cost of innovations in design.' Invoked as foil for Calleja's representational-affective-design-as-legitimate-aim defense — the closing polemic move of the chapter.

interlocutors.name: EMOTION-THEORY ABSENCES (substantive Phase 2 finding)
interlocutors.role: Damasio (2000), Ekman, Frijda, Plutchik, Tomkins, Nussbaum, Massumi, Sedgwick, Berlant, Barrett, Barsalou, Ahmed, Ngai — ALL ABSENT from this chapter despite the topic. Damasio IS cited elsewhere (Ch.10 Incorporation, p.167/169 via Lakoff + Johnson + Damasio experientialist-ontology bloc) but NOT mobilized here. Bernard Perron (game-affect theorist, anticipated by Phase 0 as likely interlocutor) is ALSO ABSENT. NO affect-theory or cognitive-emotion-science framework supplies the chapter's theoretical scaffolding — only one media-psychology construct (excitatory homeostasis) plus literary-cultural escapism theory. This documents WHAT IS MISSING per Phase 2 special guidance.

interlocutors.name: RHETORICAL-THEORY ABSENCES (substantive Phase 2 finding)
interlocutors.role: Kenneth Burke (zero hits in chapter or volume references), Aristotle (zero hits — Rhetoric II pathē would be the obvious source), Debra Hawhee (zero hits — Moving Bodies + phantasia work), Cicero / Quintilian (zero hits) — ALL ABSENT. Calleja's triple-invocation of 'rhetorical strategies of affect' (lines 4762-4764, 5119, 5156) invokes no rhetorical-theoretic tradition. This is the volume's STRONGEST single anticipatory anchor for Burkean and Aristotelian dissertation augmentation.

dimension_operational_definition: Affective involvement is the emotional-tonal modulation of player engagement — the mood-and-emotion tonality that runs through the other five PIM dimensions (kinesthetic, spatial, shared, narrative, ludic), generated via the cybernetic feedback loop between mind and machine, and crystallized as 'rhetorical strategies of affect' that may be either purposefully designed into a game or precipitated by player interpretation. Operates on macro (off-line escapism + on-ramp aesthetic anticipation) and micro (moment-to-moment designed + precipitated response) phases. (60 words.)

necessary: The medium must permit a cybernetic (recursive input/output) feedback loop combining cognitive, emotional, and kinesthetic channels — distinguishing affective involvement in games from affect-response to non-ergodic media.

Either designer-encoded rhetorical strategies (atmospherics + mechanics + AI behavior) OR player-precipitated interpretation must produce an emotional-tonal response — both fall within the dimension's scope per the closing coda.
The response need not be 'positive' — frustration, fear, panic, eeriness, shock, and the uncanny count as affective involvement; only boredom and indifference fall outside.
sufficient_indicators: Atmospheric tonality reported by player ('it's so Mirkwood'; 'serene and pretty'; 'calming'; 'I want to live there')
Mechanic-induced emotional state ('considerable panic'; 'heightened sense of urgency'; 'alerted state'; 'apprehension')
Cross-dimensional amplification: affective state heightens spatial, ludic, or shared engagement (and vice versa)
Aesthetic-habitation desire: player chooses to dwell, return to, or visit a place outside of task-motivated play
excludes: Pure mechanical-skill-improvement absent any affective dimension (Calleja treats skill-acquisition as kinesthetic, not affective)
Cognitive-strategic problem-solving without tonal modulation (treated as ludic)

Affect-response to non-ergodic media (Calleja explicitly contrasts: 'unlike non-ergodic media, in games this rhetorical power is emphasized by the conjunction of textual interpretation and the performed practice of playing,' lines 4763-4765)

paradigm_worked_examples.name: Inauro on Duskwood Forest (WoW)
paradigm_worked_examples.analytic_move: Atmospherics-as-affect-design — lighting + sound + monster placement + thematic consistency produce a 'Mirkwood' aesthetic that the player experiences as affective-evocative. Paradigm case for the chapter's secondary-world-aesthetic-evocation argument and for an anticipatory Uexküllian Merktöne (perception-tone) reading.

paradigm_worked_examples.name: Oriel on Menethil Harbor (WoW)
paradigm_worked_examples.analytic_move: Aesthetic-habitation desire as affective involvement — sunset waiting, Gadgetzan night-flying, Winterspring snow-crunching, Azshara red-and-gold leaves; 'I want to live there.' Paradigm case for habitable-secondary-world-as-affective-space.

paradigm_worked_examples.name: Aprile on Night Elf Land (WoW)
paradigm_worked_examples.analytic_move: Aesthetic-mood-regulation: 'whenever I don't feel like playing, I come here.' Paradigm case for mood-regulation-via-environment outside of task-motivated play. Anchor for the volume's clearest deliberate-non-play-affective-engagement example.

paradigm_worked_examples.name: Medal of Honor vs Red Orchestra (verisimilitude vs media-pastiche)
paradigm_worked_examples.analytic_move: Two ostensibly similar games (WWII FPS) producing 'very different affective experiences' through differential design choices: Medal of Honor draws Hollywood-pastiche affect via Spielberg/Bay film palettes + crosshair + movement-shoot accuracy; Red Orchestra draws historical-accuracy affect via no-crosshair + iron-sights + bolt-action + recoil + uniform/weapon fidelity. Paradigm case for mechanic-as-affect-source vs atmospherics-as-affect-source duality.

paradigm_worked_examples.name: Red Orchestra suppressing-fire mechanic
paradigm_worked_examples.analytic_move: Mechanic-as-designed-affect: graphical distortion + loud audio + screen-blur-on-lean-out + destructible-cover dust+fragments + historically-accurate weapon-inaccuracy → 'heightened sense of urgency, if not panic.' Calleja's clearest exhibit of designed affect at the mechanic level. Anticipatory anchor for Aristotelian pathē-as-rhetorical-strategy.

paradigm_worked_examples.name: F.E.A.R. flanking AI + light-bulb/scampering-child sequence
paradigm_worked_examples.analytic_move: Adaptive-AI-behavior as alertness generator + horror-sequence as shock+uncanniness amplifier. Prior combat-intensity amplifies subsequent horror. Cross-dimensional amplification anchor: 'leads to a more intense engagement in the spatial and ludic involvement dimensions' (lines 5072-5073).

paradigm_worked_examples.name: Left 4 Dead 2 director + Hunter cooperative-panic
paradigm_worked_examples.analytic_move: Dynamic-affect-modulation via adaptive-AI 'director' + special-zombie mechanics requiring teammate-rescue. Generates 'considerable panic' under simultaneous attack. 'Rhetorical strategies of affect tightly combine the aesthetic and systemic dimensions' (line 5119) — Calleja's strongest single statement of the dual-sourcing thesis.

layer_a_aristotelian.anchor: Aristotelian pathē (Rhetoric II) + Gross 2017 Uncomfortable Situations (Berlant cruel-optimism + Barrett constructed-emotion + Barsalou situated-conceptualization)
layer_a_aristotelian.rationale: Gross 2017 IS a confirmed corpus-index pipeline, making this the strongest dissertation-bridge in the volume. Aristotle's Rhetoric II catalogue of pathē supplies the classical-rhetorical scaffolding Calleja's triple 'rhetorical strategies of affect' formulation invokes but does not theorize: pathē are designed-rhetorical-effects produced by rhetorical situations (Aristotle's situated-affect doctrine avant la lettre). Gross's situated-affect frame then supplies what Calleja manifestly lacks: (a) a theory of how situated game-environments precipitate specific patterned affective responses (Barsalou situated-conceptualization); (b) a theory of negative-affect-as-meaningful — not arousal-tweak (Berlant cruel-optimism + Ngai ugly feelings); (c) a theory of mood-vs-emotion distinction (Barrett constructed-emotion); (d) a theory of cross-dimensional affective amplification (Gross's situated-affect across cognitive-emotional-bodily channels). The Aristotle-Gross pairing is the single most substantively extending anticipatory mapping in the volume.

layer_b_burke.anchor: Attitude (Burke's hexadic extension of the pentad — the manner/mood with which Agency is exercised; attitude as 'incipient act')
layer_b_burke.rationale: STRONGEST SINGLE ANTICIPATORY ANCHOR IN THE VOLUME per propagated IG-03 + IG-10 findings. Burke himself extended the pentad to a hexad by adding Attitude precisely to capture the affective-modal dimension of motivation (the 'how' of Agency, the manner/mood inflecting action). Calleja's affective dimension is paradigmatically the Attitude term: affect is the mood-tonality of involvement that modulates and is modulated by kinesthetic Agency, spatial Scene, shared Agents, narrative Act, and ludic Purpose. The triple-invocation of 'rhetorical strategies of affect' without invoking Burke is the volume's loudest anticipatory hook — Burke's Grammar of Motives + Hawhee's Moving Bodies (which extends Burke into bodily-rhetoric territory) jointly supply the rhetorical-theoretic scaffolding Calleja's phrasing implicitly requires.

layer_c_uexkull.anchor: Merktöne / Wirktöne (perception-tones / effect-tones in the Umwelt)
layer_c_uexkull.rationale: PROMINENT BRIDGE per plan §1.4. Uexküll's tone-doctrine holds that perceptual and effector signs are not affect-neutral data but carry intrinsic emotional-tonal coloration in the Umwelt (the tick perceives butyric acid not as molecule-data but as 'food-tone'/'attack-tone'). Calleja's atmospherics passages — Duskwood's 'dark gloomy fantasy forest' tone (Inauro), Night Elf Land's 'serene and pretty' tone (Aprile), Menethil-Harbor sunset-tone (Oriel), F.E.A.R.'s tense-and-dark atmosphere, Left 4 Dead 2's tense-and-dark director-modulated atmosphere, suppressing-fire-induced apprehension-tone — are paradigmatically tone-coloration of perception-action loops. Uexküll's framework natively integrates perception-side (Merktöne) and action-side (Wirktöne) affective tonality, resolving the chapter's atmospherics-vs-mechanics tension (T1) at the level of biosemiotic theory. The Inauro Mirkwood-evocation passage (lines 4934-4939) is the cleanest single Uexküllian-tone exhibit in the volume.

cross_pipeline_bridges.rationale: PROMINENT DISSERTATION-BRIDGE per plan §1.4. Gross's situated-affect frame supplies what Calleja manifestly lacks: theory of how situated environments precipitate specific affect (Barsalou); theory of negative affect as more than arousal-tweak (Berlant cruel-optimism + Ngai ugly feelings); theory of mood/emotion distinction (Barrett); theory of cross-dimensional affective amplification (Gross). The chapter's 'rhetorical strategies of affect' triple-invocation is a screaming anticipatory hook for affect-as-rhetoric grounding which Gross's frame would supply. Bridge cannot be anchored via shared-Gibson affordance theory (Calleja does not cite Gibson) — bridge is singly-anchored anticipatory.

Calleja's extended Tuan-on-imagination passage (lines 4814-4831) treats imagination as the faculty of 'seeing what is not there' that retains past + potential future + present-moment awareness simultaneously — paradigmatic phantasia operation in classical-rhetorical register. Tolkien's 'secondary worlds' frame (lines 4876-4889) is structurally a phantasia-of-habitable-world. Hawhee's phantasia work supplies the rhetorical-cognitive scaffolding Calleja's escapism-as-imagination treatment implicitly requires.

BCAP's analyses of Stimmung (mood / attunement) as ontologically prior to event-emotion would supply the mood-vs-emotion distinction Calleja conflates (T3). The escapism-as-imagination passages (especially Tuan-via-Calleja on 'mentally detaching ourselves temporarily from the present moment') touch ekstatic-temporal-attunement themes BCAP could ground. Anticipatory; Calleja's only Heidegger citation in the volume is QCT at p.21 (off-chapter).

Aristotle's Rhetoric II pathē catalogue supplies the classical-rhetorical scaffolding for the triple 'rhetorical strategies of affect.' Bowin AMT's aisthesis analyses bridge to the cognitive-emotional-kinesthetic feedback loop (line 4735). Anticipatory; zero Aristotle hits per Phase 0 cite-check.

Affective dimension is the PRIMARY candidate construct for dissertation empirical-adaptation. Calleja's relative under-development makes Gross-2017-via-Berlant/Barrett/Barsalou augmentation substantively extending rather than merely re-describing. The chapter is anticipatory-bridge dense rather than exegetically dense per Phase 0 design.

four_axis_confirmation.axis_1_page_count: 12 pp (135-146) — SHORTEST dimension chapter in the volume. Ch.4 (Kinesthetic) ≈18 pp; Ch.5 (Spatial) ≈20 pp; Ch.6 (Shared) ≈16 pp; Ch.7 (Narrative) ≈18 pp; Ch.9 (Ludic) ≈20 pp. Affective is roughly 33% shorter than the typical dimension treatment.
four_axis_confirmation.axis_2_subsection_count: 3 named subsections (Macro Phase: Escapism and Affect; Micro Phase: Emotional Affect during Gameplay; Aesthetics and Affect) + 1 unnamed coda. Other dimension chapters carry 4-5 named subsections. Architectural sparsity, not merely page-count sparsity.
four_axis_confirmation.axis_3_citation_density: 2 distinct emotion-theory citations (Bryant + Davies 2006; Grodal 2000) supplying ONE imported construct (excitatory homeostasis). Ch.4 Kinesthetic invokes ~7-8 distinct interlocutors (Gallagher, Merleau-Ponty-adjacent, Klevjer, et al.). The escapism interlocutors (Tuan 1998; Tolkien 1983; Evans 2001) are cultural-imagination theorists, not emotion theorists. Roughly 4x lower theorist-density than Ch.4.
four_axis_confirmation.axis_4_theoretical_framework: No affect-theoretic framework (Massumi, Sedgwick, Berlant, Ahmed, Ngai), no cognitive-emotion-science framework (Damasio — present in Ch.10 but absent here, Ekman, Frijda, Plutchik, Barrett, Barsalou, Tomkins), no phenomenology of mood (Heidegger Stimmung, Schmitz atmosphere-philosophy), no rhetorical-theoretic tradition (Burke, Aristotle, Hawhee) despite three uses of 'rhetorical strategies of affect.' The chapter's theoretical scaffolding is media-psychology (one construct) + literary-cultural escapism theory (three voices).

what_is_missing: No engagement with Antonio Damasio despite Damasio appearing later in the volume (Ch.10 Incorporation, p.167/169, in the Lakoff+Johnson+Damasio experientialist-ontology bloc). The Ch.10 mobilization of Damasio for incorporation-grounding makes the Ch.8 non-mobilization for affect-grounding a NOTABLE NON-USE.

No engagement with Paul Ekman (basic-emotion theory), Nico Frijda (emotion as action-readiness — would have been directly relevant to the cybernetic-feedback-loop framing), Robert Plutchik (emotion-wheel), Silvan Tomkins (affect theory).

No engagement with the affect-theory tradition: Brian Massumi (affect/emotion split — directly relevant to T3 mood-vs-emotion tension), Eve Sedgwick (Touching Feeling), Lauren Berlant (cruel optimism — directly relevant to negative-affect-as-legitimate), Sara Ahmed (Cultural Politics of Emotion), Sianne Ngai (Ugly Feelings — directly relevant to frustration-as-engagement-driver).

No engagement with phenomenology of mood: Heidegger's Stimmung / Befindlichkeit (which would have grounded the mood-as-environmental-attunement reading of WoW aesthetic-mood-regulation), Hermann Schmitz / Gernot Böhme atmosphere-philosophy (which would have grounded the atmospherics-as-affect-source argument).

No engagement with rhetorical theory despite triple-invocation of 'rhetorical strategies of affect': no Burke (pentad / Attitude / Grammar of Motives), no Aristotle (Rhetoric II pathē), no Hawhee (Moving Bodies / phantasia / rhetorical bodies), no Cicero/Quintilian on movere.
No mood/emotion distinction — the two terms are deployed interchangeably as paired-noun construction throughout the chapter; theoretically load-bearing distinction is flattened.
No theory of cross-dimensional affective amplification — the phenomenon is repeatedly observed (three discrete passages) but no mechanism account is supplied.

No theory of negative-affect-as-meaningful beyond 'better than boredom' — the affect-theory tradition since Sedgwick and Ngai treats negative affect as substantively generative, but this is not engaged.
No engagement with Csikszentmihalyi flow theory despite topical adjacency — confirmed Phase 0 flag.
No engagement with Bernard Perron's game-affect work (anticipated by Phase 0 manifest seed as likely interlocutor).
No invocation of Freud's Unheimlich despite Calleja's use of 'uncanny' (line 5085) and 'uncanniness' (line 5156).

rhetorical_strategies_of_affect_location.context: Macro Phase opening — 'Game design, like other forms of textual production, is imbued with the rhetorical strategies of affect. But unlike non-ergodic media, in games this rhetorical power is emphasized by the conjunction of textual interpretation and the performed practice of playing.'
rhetorical_strategies_of_affect_location.anticipatory_anchor: Burke pentadic Attitude (the rhetorical 'how' / manner of motive) + Aristotle Rhetoric II pathē (designed-rhetorical-effects). Calleja's textual-production/non-ergodic-media contrast invites a Burke/Hawhee rhetoric-of-bodies-and-acts extension.

rhetorical_strategies_of_affect_location.context: Aesthetics and Affect / Left 4 Dead 2 analysis — 'Left 4 Dead 2 creates such an evocative experience because its rhetorical strategies of affect tightly combine the aesthetic and systemic dimensions.'
rhetorical_strategies_of_affect_location.anticipatory_anchor: STRONGEST occurrence for Burke + Uexküll + Gross augmentation. The 'aesthetic + systemic' dual-sourcing is paradigmatically Uexküllian (Merktöne + Wirktöne dual tonality) AND Burkean (Attitude as the modulator that integrates Scene-rhetoric and Agency-rhetoric) AND Grossian (situated-affect across perceptual + action channels).

rhetorical_strategies_of_affect_location.context: Coda — 'This dimension accounts for the rhetorical strategies of affect that are either purposefully designed into a game or precipitated by the individual player's interpretation of in-game events and interactions with other players.'
rhetorical_strategies_of_affect_location.anticipatory_anchor: Definitional crystallization — the dimension itself is what 'accounts for the rhetorical strategies of affect.' The designed/precipitated distinction (Burke: designer-rhetorical-motive vs received-attitude; Aristotle: rhetorical-situation vs hearer-disposition; Gross: situation-priming vs situated-conceptualization-by-subject) is the chapter's terminological signature.
